title: Could not deploy latest (v1.6.0) airbyte community with abctl. Same version used to work last week.
body:
### Helm Chart Version

1.6.0

### What step the error happened?

On deploy

### Relevant information

I'm trying to create a brand new GCE instance with airbyte using abctl and the deployement is unable to complete with the following info in log:
```
...
 WARNING  Encountered an issue deploying Airbyte:                               
            Pod: airbyte-abctl-workload-launcher-5b6cb9cf97-ngntn.18386e77b4a2e0bf
            Reason: Failed
            Message: Error: couldn't find key dataplane-client-id in Secret airbyte-abctl/airbyte-auth-secrets
            Count: 8
  DEBUG   helm: Deployment is not ready: airbyte-abctl/airbyte-abctl-workload-launcher. 0 out of 1 expected pods are ready
```
It just keeps throwing that last message with no progress.

Exactly the same configuration (including GCE config and OS, i'm using terraform to build it) worked at the beginning on last week and I have one instance running as a proof.

Here are my config files:
```
cat << EOF > secret.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: airbyte-config-secrets
type: Opaque
stringData:
  database-user: admin
  database-password: "${db_password}"
EOF
cat << EOF > values.yaml
global:
  auth:
    cookieSecureSetting: "false"
  env_vars:
    HTTP_IDLE_TIMEOUT: "10m"
    READ_TIMEOUT: "10m"
    AIRBYTE_API_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: "90"
    AIRBYTE_API_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: "600"
    WORKLOAD_API_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: "600"
    MAX_CHECK_WORKERS: "12"
    MAX_DISCOVER_WORKERS: "24"
    MAX_SPEC_WORKERS: "24"
    MAX_SYNC_WORKERS: "24"
  database:
    type: external
    secretName: "airbyte-config-secrets"
    host: "${postgres_instance_host}"
    port: "5432"
    database: "${airbyte_instance_name}"
    userSecretKey: "database-user"
    passwordSecretKey: "database-password"
postgresql:
  enabled: false
EOF
```


Complete log is attached.
[abctl_install.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19839801/abctl_install.log)

comments.author: huang-pan-cryptopond
comments.body:
Linking Airbyte Community Slack message with potential fix:

https://airbytehq.slack.com/archives/C021JANJ6TY/p1745185270307599?thread_ts=1744807764.102749&cid=C021JANJ6TY

I checked the failing database migration that causes problems in the upgrade to v1.6.0. I think I found the bug. The issue lies in [this](https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte-platform/blob/42d686605b5b1eece7fe8f90675b746ecb54505a/airbyte-db/db-lib/src/main/java/io/airbyte/db/instance/configs/migrations/V1_1_1_016__AddDataplaneGroupIdToConnection.java#L61) line of code. It updates the dataplane_group_id column on the connection table ONLY where the geography column in the connection table is equal to the name column of the dataplane_group table. There is, however, only 1 record for the dataplane_group with 1 value for name field (e.g. AUTO) while different connections can have different values (EU, US, AUTO) for the geography  field. In short: connections which do not match this condition will get a NULL value for dataplane_group_id which causes the ERROR. I can think of two ways to fix this:
Enforce all Airbyte users to configure the geography field of ALL Airbyte connections to the geography value of the workspace (SELECT geography FROM workspace).
Create a dataplane_group for each geography value (EU, US, AUTO) so the migration will not result in records with NULL values.
Can you forward this to the engineering team? It might save them some time :wink: (edited)

comments.author: bgroff
comments.body:
Sorry for the delay here. You can work around this issue by doing the following (you will need Kind and Kubectl installed)

`kind export kubeconfig -n airbyte-abctl`
`kubectl exec -it -n airbyte-abctl airbyte-db-0 -- /bin/bash`
`psql -U airbyte db-airbyte`
`delete from dataplane_client_credentials ;`
`delete from dataplane;`
`\q`
`exit`

Then run the abctl install again. This should recreated the dataplane and its credentials and put them in the correct place. The team is working on getting 1.6.1 out in the next couple of days.

comments.author: Blessedadudu
comments.body:
Run 

` abctl local install --insecure-cookies -v `

This tries to install 1.6.0 by default, you would be stuck with the dataplane issue. Then run these

```
export KUBECONFIG="$HOME/.airbyte/abctl/abctl.kubeconfig"

kubectl exec -it -n airbyte-abctl airbyte-db-0 -- /bin/bash

psql -U airbyte db-airbyte

delete from dataplane_client_credentials ;

delete from dataplane;

\q
exit
```

Don't uninstall. Just run this again

`abctl local install --insecure-cookies -v `

Give it some time. The -v shows the logs as installations go on. Wait a little. This is what I did.

comments.body:
For those facing this problem **Failed to obtain or add dataplane access token**:

I did some extensive testing/troubleshooting because i was facing the same problem. It seems that the main problem here is to have the secret **airbyte-auth-secrets** pre-created.

I tried to get the values of the dataplane client id and secret directly from the database and updating my secret with it, but it not worked. Somehow, having the secret pre-created and managed externally, the secret was not being updated even though i have configured the role to do so.

Using helm charts v1, and with version 1.8.5 without being able to make the workload-launcher health, I commented out these fields:
- global.auth.instanceAdmin.secretName (set to airbyte-auth-secrets)
- global.auth.instanceAdmin.emailSecretKey (set to instance-admin-email)
- global.auth.instanceAdmin.passwordSecretKey (set to instance-admin-password)

And also the definitions of my airbyte-auth-secrets managed secret.

After that, I deleted the existing secret from the cluster and deployed the changes. Airbyte was able to create the secret by itself (somehow it kept the same values for the instance admin keys), but also created the dataplane-client-id and dataplane-client-secret. And then the workload-launcher was able to launch.

Validated with:

curl -v --request POST \
  --url https://URL/api/v1/dataplanes/token \
  --header 'accept: application/json' \
  --header 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "client_id": "BASE64_DECODED_DATAPLANE_CLIENT_ID",
    "client_secret": "BASE64_DECODED_DATAPLANE_CLIENT_SECRET"
  }'

...
{"access_token":"..."}

where it used to be

{"message":"Internal Server Error: Service account not found: 1abb44f8-...-dd38595a1096","exceptionClassName":"io.airbyte.data.services.ServiceAccountNotFound","exceptionStack":[],"rootCauseExceptionStack":[]}

Hope this helps! **Consider using version 1.8.x as it fixes some bugs related to this dataplane thing**.
